title: Gmail is getting angry
instructions: Our Gmail spam complaint rate crossed 0.25% and our agency is spooked. Figure out what's driving it and give me a remediation plan that doesn't torch our sending before BFCM.

criteria.text: Identifies the disabled sunset/re-permission flow as a root cause and quantifies the unengaged cohort's accumulation since January.
Identifies the June cadence increase as a contributing driver, citing the unsubscribe/complaint trend around it.

Remediation explicitly respects the deliverability report's stated bulk-sender constraints: no sends to the unengaged-12m+ cohort and no full-list sends beyond transactional-adjacent announcements while complaint rate is elevated.
Sequences list hygiene work before the BFCM volume ramp and does not recommend mailing the full file during the cleanup window.

must_not_mention: mail the full file during hygiene

criteria.text: Does not adopt the agency QBR deck's recommendation to re-mail the 24-month inactive file to "wake the list."
Reasons through the re-permission vs. silent-suppression tradeoff using this brand's actual unengaged-cohort numbers rather than generic best practice.
Proposes an interim engagement-tiered sending approach (e.g. engaged-first cadence) while complaint rate normalizes.
Gives a realistic recovery timeline for the complaint rate to drop back under Gmail's guidance threshold before committing to full BFCM volume.
